originality.rationale: The normalizer-index refined counts are not equivalent to the dimension-only subalgebra and ideal zeta functions: distinct nonideal subalgebras can have equal dimensions but distinct normalizer codimensions. The full text of Lee, arXiv:2010.02268, section 5.1, Theorem 5.1 and Example 5.2, explicitly enumerates ideals only in this family, recovering the Y=0 specialization but not the mixed Y-coefficients. Lee--Voll, arXiv:2006.12346, examines subrepresentations and ideal/submodule zeta functions rather than normalizer filtration. Published-nearby and existing mathematical results retrieved for this algebra family concern commuting graphs, retractions, and related invariants, not this joint census. The Gaussian incidence factor is classical and not itself claimed as new; exact historical priority remains subject to the listed risk.
